title: Common K-flat representatives for the two etale coefficient-counit composites
statement:
Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, separated finite-type $k$-schemes $U,V$, a separated etale finite-type $k$-morphism $e:U\to V$, and a unital map $\varphi:A\to B$ of finite commutative rings killed by powers of $\ell$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Work on small ordinary etale sites in the constant-ring derived categories with localization $Q_R$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Write $S_R=e_{\Sigma!,R}$, $E_R=DS_R$, and $v_R:E_Re_R^*\to1$ for the degreewise sum adjunction counit [def-weil-pbc-etale-sum-extension, lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality]. Use the sheaf counits $v_R^0$, ordinary scalar/pullback map $a^0$ and summandwise tensor map $\rho$ of [lem-sp-etale-sheaf-fold-scalar]. Let $T_T=-\otimes^L_{A_T}B_T$ be canonical scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], $\sigma_e:T_VE_A\xrightarrow{\sim}E_BT_U$ the specified comparison [lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility], and $a_e:T_Ue_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}e_B^*T_V$ the inverse of the representative-normalized scalar/pullback comparison [def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso].
Let $K$ be bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude on $V$, and assume $e_A^*K$ is in the same class on $U$, with constructibility and Tor amplitude as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf, def-kun-tor-amplitude]. Let $K_0$ be any representing cochain complex, $P\to K_0$ a quasi-isomorphism with $P$ K-flat and flat termwise, and $\eta:Q_AP\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ the induced isomorphism [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-quasi-iso-modules, def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules].
Then $e_A^*P$ and $S_Ae_A^*P$ are K-flat with flat terms. The canonical K-flat computation isomorphisms give
$$\lambda_P:Q_B((S_Ae_A^*P)\otimes_A B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_V(E_Ae_A^*K),\qquad \tau_P:Q_B(P\otimes_A B)\xrightarrow{\sim}T_VK.$$
Define the two chain maps with common source and target by
$$f_P=v^0_{B,P\otimes_A B}\circ S_B(a_P^0)\circ\rho_{e_A^*P},\qquad g_P=v^0_{A,P}\otimes1_B.$$
The specified derived maps are represented by these particular chain maps, in the precise sense
$$\tau_P\circ Q_B(f_P)=\bigl(v_{B,T_VK}\circ E_B(a_e(K))\circ\sigma_e(e_A^*K)\bigr)\circ\lambda_P,$$
$$\tau_P\circ Q_B(g_P)=T_V(v_{A,K})\circ\lambda_P.$$
The identifications are compatible with chain maps between such resolutions and with transport along $\eta$, and therefore independent of the chosen flat-term K-flat resolution. No flatness or finite projective dimension of $B$ over $A$ is assumed. This assertion identifies the two composites separately; it does not assert their equality.

Apply this to P and J and compose with the given representing isomorphism eta to construct exactly the prescribed inverses of lambda and tau.

proof.text: The counit formula for the total-derived adjunction on a homotopy representative agrees with the counit formula for localization of the complex adjunction. Extensionality for transformations out of localization and adjunction extensionality identify these two adjunctions. The scalar/pullback inverse is the mate of the exact restriction-of-scalars square: transport the known normalized mate through the left-derived/exact inverse-image isomorphisms. Iterated mates then show that the specified first derived composite is scalar extension of the A-counit. The reused private helpers from the open-comparison modules are generic category-theoretic mate identities, with no open-immersion hypothesis.

proof.text: The existing ordinary fold comparison identifies the two specified chain maps. For the second chain map, apply naturality of the scalar representative to the degreewise A-counit and use the localization counit formula. Naturality of the derived counit transports this identity along eta. Combine this calculation with the two fold equalities to obtain the first equation as well.

source.place: Charts: integral summation and compatibility with extension of coefficients

proof.text: The degreewise extended fold is a natural transformation, so both chain maps are natural. The exact source comparison followed by the scalar representative is itself natural. An elementary conjugation lemma for natural transformations and prescribed inverse computation maps proves both transport assertions. Finally each transported chain composite equals the same fixed scalar-extended derived counit; cancelling the computation isomorphisms gives resolution independence, without a third resolution.

This is a first split of lem-sp-etale-counit-scalar-model, which N0 created on 2026-10-22 under lem-sp-etale-sum-counit-scalar. It adds 0 new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged: it matches all earlier snapshots, and live and side-live still show the item unsplit. No re-split note exists. Steps: Step 1 gets K-flat flat-term H=e_A^*P from lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat (the 0G7E content), using c:e^{-1}A_V≅A_U from prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact(1),(2); it gets the same for J=S_AH from lem-pur-etale-sum-flat-kflat. Step 2 builds λ,τ from exact factors and the K-flat computation r of lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings. Step 3: σ_e's summandwise K-flat normalization gives E_B(r_H)σ_e r_J^{-1}=Q(ρ_H). I checked the direction by hand: def-pur-etale-scalar-pullback-iso's c;S(g);r=Lf^*(r_P);g;Q(a_P), with a_P:e_B^*P_B→H_B, inverts to e_B^*(r_P)a_e r_H^{-1}=Q(a_P^{-1})=Q(a^0_P). Step 4: naturality of v_B at r_P, together with def-weil-exact-derived-adjunction's localized counit, gives Q(f_P). I checked every factor, and the fold equality is not used. Step 5: naturality of r at v^0_{A,P}:J→P gives the g identity. Step 6: Φ_K is natural in K because σ_e, a_e and v are natural, which gives transport along η; resolution independence comes from 06YY-style canonical comparison. Source: the blueprint Charts paragraph ('summation over fibres is defined integrally'), plus Stacks 0G7E (line 3508) and 06YY (line 3585), read. Edge cases e=id, U empty, U=V⊔V and nonflat Z/ℓ²→F_ℓ are all consistent. Off-unit uses (lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality, lem-sp-et-proet-coefficient-compatibility) are recorded and not refused, and both are already among the parent's tools. The new generic tools are declared in split_report.tool_uses for the maintainer (C8). Minor: the report mentions a citations.json that was not delivered; this has no effect on the DAG. No fixes.
